# Quick start

Start a NocoBase application, describe your business to an AI Agent, and begin building your system. This guide uses Northstar Logistics to create customers, drivers, transport orders, and a workspace with one prompt. Later chapters extend the same application with more capabilities.

## Prepare your AI Agent

Prepare a Coding Agent, Node.js 24 or later, and pnpm 11. Use a Bash terminal, or WSL on Windows, to install the global NocoBase 3 Skills:

```bash
npx skills@latest add nocobase/skills-v3 --skill '*' -g
```

Select your Coding Agent when prompted, then start a new Agent session to load the installed Skills. The [lightweight distribution repository](https://github.com/nocobase/skills-v3) provides these Skills, including application creation guidance.

Creating an application synchronizes its development Skills into `.agents/skills/` in the application directory. Start a new session in that directory so the Agent can follow the application’s `AGENTS.md` and project Skills for development.

## 1. Create and start the application

In the directory where you keep projects, run this command to obtain the creation tool and default application template from the npm beta channel and install dependencies:

```bash
PNPM_CONFIG_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0 pnpm create @nocobase/app@beta northstar-logistics --template-tag=beta
```

Enter the application directory, initialize its configuration, and start it. This example uses SQLite, which requires no separate database service:

```bash
cd northstar-logistics
pnpm nocobase config init --dialect sqlite
pnpm nocobase config check
pnpm dev
```

Open the application URL printed in the terminal and sign in with the administrator account configured during initialization. An Agent can also complete these steps for you using the installed `nocobase-create-app` Skill.

## 2. Build the business with one prompt

Northstar Logistics provides regional transportation and delivery services to business customers. It needs to manage customers, drivers, and transport orders, while helping dispatchers find orders that need a driver.

Start an AI Agent session with the new application directory as its working directory and send this request:

```text
Build a transport management application for Northstar Logistics with four pages: Workspace, Transport orders, Customers, and Drivers. Use a blue theme and left sidebar navigation.
The workspace shows four statistics: total orders, awaiting dispatch, customers, and completed orders, plus stage distribution, orders awaiting dispatch, and recent orders.
Support order search, stage filtering, creation, editing, and driver assignment. Order details show the customer, route, cargo, owner, fee, and expected delivery. Customer and driver pages include lists, details, and related orders.
Add English demo data with 10 orders, 4 customers, and 4 drivers across different transport stages. Connect the statistics, lists, and details to the same data.
```

The Agent builds the data model, business pages, and navigation. Once it finishes, open the application to see the result.

## 3. View the result

### Transport workspace

The workspace brings together total orders, orders awaiting dispatch, customers, and completed orders. Stage distribution shows overall progress, and the dispatch list highlights orders that need a driver. Recent orders link to their details.

This example contains ten orders and four customers. Statistics and lists use the application's order data.

![Northstar transport workspace with statistics, stage distribution, dispatch priorities, and recent orders](./assets/northstar-workspace-en.png)

**The workspace brings statistics, stages and pending orders together.**

### Order details

Open **NS-2026-001** to view its customer, route, cargo, owner, fee, and expected delivery. This order is awaiting dispatch, with editing and driver assignment available.

![Northstar order details and driver assignment](./assets/northstar-order-detail-en.png)

**Order details show business information with editing and driver-assignment entries.**

The application now has baseline customer, driver, and order management pages. Continue describing business needs to add branded sign-in, role permissions, transport workflows, approvals, attachments, and messages in the same application.

## Extend the same application

Later chapters introduce capabilities through Northstar's transport operations. Account managers record requirements, dispatchers assign drivers, drivers deliver goods and upload proof of delivery, operations supervisors monitor progress, and finance reviews additional transport costs.

| Role                      | Responsibilities                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Account manager           | Maintain customers, create transport orders, track deliveries, and communicate with customers. |
| Dispatcher                | Assign drivers and resolve delays.                                                             |
| Driver                    | Handle assigned transport tasks and upload proof of delivery.                                  |
| Operations supervisor     | Monitor progress and review special transport requests.                                        |
| Finance reviewer          | Review additional costs and relevant financial information.                                    |
| Application administrator | Manage access and inspect scheduled tasks and delivery logs.                                   |

Authentication brings employees into the system, authorization controls which orders each role can access and handle, and workflows advance transport operations. Files, notifications, and email support collaboration. Scheduled reminders, external data sources, languages, and themes are added as business needs arise.

The Agent integrates these capabilities and builds business pages and management interfaces around the company's working practices.

# Overview

NocoBase provides reusable capabilities for business applications. Describe your business goals to an AI Agent, which integrates authentication, authorization, data, processes, and collaboration into application-owned pages.

## Available capabilities

| Capability                                         | Purpose                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Authentication](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md)                 | Password and corporate sign-in, sessions, API keys, and branded sign-in pages.                                |
| [Data sources](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/data-sources.md)                  | Application databases and existing external database connections.                                             |
| [Authorization](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/authorization/index.md)          | Page, action, and record access, default access, sharing, restrictions, and inspection.                       |
| [Lifecycles](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/workflow/index.md)                  | Business stages, human actions, external results, time limits, and transition history.                        |
| [Approval](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/approval/index.md)                    | Multi-stage and multi-person approval rules and collaboration.                                                |
| [Task Center](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/task-center.md)                    | Bring approvals, equipment collection and other personal work together with shared status filters and counts. |
| [Files](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/file.md)                                 | Upload, association, preview, download, storage, and access control.                                          |
| [Notifications](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/notification.md)                 | Business messages through inbox, email, or group channels, with delivery records.                             |
| [Email](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/index.md)                           | Personal mailboxes, correspondence, signatures, templates, and business integration.                          |
| [Scheduled tasks](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/scheduler.md)                  | Reminders, reports, synchronization, execution records, and enablement controls.                              |
| [Languages](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/i18n.md)                             | Language switching, translations, and application defaults.                                                   |
| [Themes](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/theme.md)                               | Colors, typography, density, color modes, and custom presets.                                                 |
| [AI employees](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-employee/index.md)             | AI collaboration with models, tools, and business context.                                                    |
| [AI knowledge bases](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/index.md) | Knowledge content and retrieval for AI.                                                                       |

Requirements differ by capability: external mail needs provider configuration, and complex approval needs its plugin. Application pages follow business needs rather than requiring a shared settings area.

## Reading this chapter

Start with the [quick start](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/quick-start.md), to create the application and build a transport workspace, then follow the Northstar Logistics journey or use the sidebar to find a capability.

# Authentication

Authentication identifies people accessing an application. After sign-in, a session identifies the current user. [Authorization](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/authorization/index.md) determines which data and business actions that user can access.

## Available capabilities

| Capability                                                               | What it provides                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Password authentication and accounts](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/password.md)                    | Username or email and password sign-in, registration controls, password requirements, recovery, and sign-in status. |
| [Accounts and sessions](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/password.md#company-managed-employee-accounts) | Create or disable employee accounts, sign out, and revoke existing sessions.                                        |
| [API keys](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/api-keys.md)                                                | Credentials for scripts and integrations, with expiry and revocation.                                               |
| [Additional sign-in methods](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/sign-in-methods.md)                       | Corporate identity providers, third-party accounts, and other authentication methods.                               |
| [Protected pages and APIs](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/protecting-access.md)                       | Public and authenticated pages, and current-user identity in APIs.                                                  |
| [Custom sign-in pages](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/login-pages.md)                                 | Company names, logos, backgrounds, layouts, and colors.                                                             |

## Where to start

Begin with [Password authentication and accounts](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/password.md) to learn how employees sign in and out and how accounts and sessions are managed. Explore API keys, additional sign-in methods, and protected access as needed, then [Customize the sign-in page](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/login-pages.md) to adapt its background, branding and layout.

# Password authentication and accounts

[← Authentication overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md) · [Open the related scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#staff)

Northstar account managers, dispatchers, and drivers sign in with company-managed accounts. Administrators create accounts and disable them when employees leave.

> This guide demonstrates a customized Northstar application. Authentication supplies password sign-in and sessions; employee management screens are built for the business, and password recovery requires a working email channel.

[Sign in and sign out](#sign-in-and-sign-out) · [Company-managed employee accounts](#company-managed-employee-accounts) · [Custom password requirements](#custom-password-requirements) · [Recover a password](#recover-a-password)

## Sign in and sign out

Enter a username or email and password, then click **Sign in**. This example uses the blue Northstar sign-in page with NocoBase authentication and sessions.

![Sign in to Northstar](../assets/northstar-password-login-en.png)

After signing in, open the avatar menu in the upper-right corner and choose **Sign out**. You return to the sign-in page. Sign in again when your session expires.

![Sign out from the employee menu](../assets/northstar-password-signout-en.png)

See [Customize sign-in pages](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/login-pages.md) for branding and layout changes.

## Company-managed employee accounts

Internal applications can disable public self-registration and let administrators create and manage accounts. Restrict account creation on both the page and the server.

```text
Northstar’s transport system is for company employees only.
Disable self-registration on both the sign-in page and the server.
Build an Employee accounts page for administrators, with name/email search and enabled/disabled filters.
Support creating, disabling, and enabling accounts, and revoking sessions separately.
Keep account creation separate from business permission assignment. Never grant administrator access by default.
```

Open **Employee accounts** to see each employee’s name, email, username, permission sets, and status. Click **New employee** and enter a name, email, and initial password. A username is optional.

![Employee account list](../assets/northstar-employee-accounts-en.png)

An account lets an employee sign in; permission sets determine which business records they can access. Creating an account does not grant access to all orders. See [Roles and permissions](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/authorization/index.md).

## Custom password requirements

Applications can customize password requirements and validate them consistently during account creation and resets. Explain the requirements in the form; this example uses a minimum of 12 characters.

```text
Require at least 12 characters when setting or resetting a password.
Show the requirement in account creation and password reset forms, with matching server-side validation.
Existing employees can continue signing in with their current passwords without an immediate password change.
```

The account creation form displays the minimum length. Enter a shorter password and click **Create** to see the validation message. The account is not submitted. The server also validates new passwords.

![Minimum password length validation](../assets/northstar-password-policy-en.png)

## Recover a password

Users who forget passwords can reset them through their registered email without administrator intervention. Confirm email ownership and provide an expiring reset link.

```text
Add a forgot-password flow for Northstar employees using an email channel.
Let employees choose Forgot password? and enter their email.
Show the same submission message whether or not an account exists.
Use the email link to set a password of at least 12 characters and return to sign-in.
Reuse authentication’s expiring, single-use reset links.
```

Click **Forgot password?** and enter the account email.

![Forgot-password form](../assets/northstar-forgot-password-en.png)

A working email delivery channel is required to complete the request → email → reset link → new password flow. The email link must point to an application address the employee can reach.

## Sessions and disabled accounts

Offboarding, suspended accounts or revoked access require blocking future sign-ins and invalidating existing sessions. Disable accounts while preserving associated business records, with the option to enable them again.

```text
Add an employee offboarding action for administrators.
Show the employee name and consequences before confirmation.
After confirmation, prevent sign-in and revoke existing sessions while preserving business records.
Allow re-enabling the account, requiring the employee to sign in again.
```

Open Taylor’s row menu and choose **Disable**. The confirmation explains that sign-in will be blocked and existing sessions revoked, while business records remain available.

![Confirm employee offboarding](../assets/northstar-disable-confirm-en.png)

After confirmation, Taylor’s status becomes **Disabled**. Existing sessions cannot access internal business resources, and the employee returns to sign-in. Choose **Enable** to restore account availability; revoked sessions are not restored.

![Disabled employee account](../assets/northstar-disabled-account-en.png)

Use **Revoke sessions** to require a new sign-in without disabling the account. See [Protect pages and APIs](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/protecting-access.md) for public and internal access.

## Verify the result

- Search, filter, and create employee accounts.
- Self-registration is disabled in both the interface and server.
- Disabling an account revokes existing sessions while preserving business records.
- Forms explain the minimum length of 12 characters.
- Both client and server reject new passwords that do not meet the rule.
- Existing employees can still sign in with their current passwords.
- A real mailbox receives a reset link using the correct application URL.
- The new password works and the old password no longer signs in.
- Expired or used links cannot be reused, and unknown emails do not reveal account existence.

Return to the [related overview scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#staff) to adapt the prompt and continue with your Agent.

# API keys

[← Authentication overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md) · [Open the related scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#api)

An API key lets scripts, scheduled tasks, and external systems call application APIs without browser sign-in. By default, it represents its creator and uses that user’s existing permissions.

A Northstar account manager can use a Key to send accessible transport orders to a reporting system, while continuing to use the application through browser sign-in.

> API keys provide programmatic credentials. The integration-key screen and order API below belong to the Northstar example; verify the actual endpoints, response fields, and user permissions in your application.

[Provide an integration keys entry](#provide-an-integration-keys-entry) · [Create, save, and revoke](#create-save-and-revoke) · [Read transport orders with a script](#read-transport-orders-with-a-script) · [Result](#result)

## Provide an integration keys entry

Scripts and external systems can use separate API credentials instead of storing user passwords. Set key expiration and revoke credentials when the integration ends.

Management pages can follow business needs without a shared Settings entry:

```text
Add an Integration keys entry to the Northstar user menu using the existing API keys capability.
Employees manage only their own Keys.
Creation accepts a purpose name, such as Transport reporting, and an expiry.
Show the full Key only once after creation and ask the employee to copy it immediately.
List names, identifying fragments, status, expiry, and last use. Support revocation with confirmation.
Never expose full Keys in lists, logs, or later detail views.
```

The capability handles Keys, expiry, and revocation; the application defines page location and layout. Employees need permission to access the entry.

## Create, save, and revoke

Open Integration keys, supply a purpose and expiry, and save the full value in the calling program’s runtime environment. It appears only once; an identifying fragment cannot recover it.

Revoke a Key when it is no longer needed. Revoked or expired Keys cannot continue calling APIs; create another for a new integration. A disabled account’s Keys cannot keep representing that account.

## Read transport orders with a script

Use API requests to process application data with scripts instead of manually exporting or copying it. Access retains the key owner’s permission scope.

Save the Key in the program’s `NOCOBASE_API_KEY` environment variable:

```text
Write a script to read Northstar transport orders.
Read the API key from NOCOBASE_API_KEY, never source code or logs.
Use the application's actual API documentation to select the order list endpoint and send the Key in the x-api-key header.
The example app is http://localhost:13200/main. GET /api/northstar returns workspace data; data.orders contains accessible orders.
Read orders, resolve customer names using data.customers, and output order number, customer, origin, destination, and status.
Handle API failures instead of treating them as an empty order list.
Explain how to configure the application address and run the script.
```

This example uses a Key created by Alice, an account manager. The script calls `GET /main/api/northstar` with the `x-api-key` header, extracts orders from the workspace response, and resolves customer names. This endpoint returns accessible workspace records in a single response, without pagination.

> This script targets the Northstar example API, not a universal NocoBase orders endpoint. Check paths, response structure, and pagination before using it with another application.

### Run the script

Save the code as `fetch_orders.py`. It uses only the Python standard library.

```python
import json
import os
import sys
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

base_url = os.environ["NOCOBASE_APP_URL"].rstrip("/")
request = Request(
    base_url + "/api/northstar",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["NOCOBASE_API_KEY"]},
)
try:
    with urlopen(request, timeout=20) as response:
        result = json.load(response)
    data = result["data"]
    customers = {str(item["id"]): item["name"] for item in data["customers"]}
    orders = [
        {
            "number": order["number"],
            "customer": customers.get(str(order["customerId"]), ""),
            "origin": order["origin"],
            "destination": order["destination"],
            "status": order["status"],
        }
        for order in data["orders"]
    ]
except HTTPError as error:
    sys.exit(f"API request failed: HTTP {error.code}")
except URLError:
    sys.exit("Cannot reach the application API.")
except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
    sys.exit("Unexpected API response format.")

print(json.dumps({"count": len(orders), "orders": orders}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
```

Set the application address, enter the copied Key, and run:

```bash
export NOCOBASE_APP_URL='http://localhost:13200/main'
read -rs -p 'API key: ' NOCOBASE_API_KEY
export NOCOBASE_API_KEY
python3 fetch_orders.py
```

The `read -rs` command hides the Key as you enter it. Replace the application address and endpoint when using another application.

### Read the returned orders

The real execution returned 6 orders accessible to Alice. The first two records are shown below:

```json
{
  "count": 6,
  "orders": [
    {
      "number": "NS-2026-001",
      "customer": "Harbor Retail",
      "origin": "Shanghai",
      "destination": "Hangzhou",
      "status": "awaitingDispatch"
    },
    {
      "number": "NS-2026-002",
      "customer": "Summit Electronics",
      "origin": "Hangzhou",
      "destination": "Suzhou",
      "status": "awaitingDispatch"
    }
  ]
}
```

The orders belong to Harbor Retail and Summit Electronics; `awaitingDispatch` means awaiting dispatch. A reporting or synchronization program can use these records without browser sign-in.

A Key does not expand its owner’s data access. Give an integration account appropriate permissions for cross-team reporting. A revoked or expired Key, or a disabled account, cannot continue calling APIs. Failed requests report an HTTP status instead of appearing to be an empty order list.

See [Authorization](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/authorization/index.md) for business permissions and data scopes.

## Result

The integration keys page lists the purpose, recognizable fragment, status, expiration, and last use. This example uses a 30-day lifetime.

![Transport reporting integration key](../assets/northstar-keys-en.png)

The creation view displays the full key once. Its value is masked in this screenshot.

![One-time key display](../assets/northstar-key-created-en.png)

## Verify the result

- The script returns the expected order fields within the user's scope.
- The Key comes from the environment and never appears in code or logs.
- Revoked or expired credentials produce an error rather than an empty success result.

Return to the [related overview scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#api) to adapt the prompt and continue with your Agent.

# Adding sign-in methods

[← Authentication overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md) · [Open the related scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#sso)

Northstar employees can use the company identity provider to enter the transport application. The provider verifies their identity; the application creates its own session and applies business permissions afterward.

> This guide uses OIDC as an example. Prepare an independent identity provider and account-linking rules first. Company sign-in is not enabled in the default application.

[Supported integration approaches](#supported-integration-approaches) · [Prepare the integration](#prepare-the-integration) · [Corporate sign-in example](#corporate-sign-in-example) · [Other integration needs](#other-integration-needs)

## Supported integration approaches

Authentication is built on Better Auth and can use provider configuration or authentication extensions. These approaches require configuration; they are not all enabled in a new application.

| Need                                  | Approach                                         | Preparation                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| GitHub or Google accounts             | Provider sign-in configuration                   | Provider application, credentials, callback               |
| Corporate identity                    | OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC)               | Identity provider, application information, account rules |
| Feishu or DingTalk accounts           | Platform authorization and user information APIs | Platform application, permissions, callback               |
| Email codes or sign-in links          | Authentication extension                         | Mail service, pages, storage                              |
| Passkeys or two-factor authentication | Authentication extension                         | Pages, configuration, data structures                     |
| Internal tickets or signatures        | Custom authentication extension                  | Protocol, verification API, stable identity               |

## Prepare the integration

The identity administrator registers the transport application, provides provider details and credentials, and registers the callback. The Agent implements application-side integration; credentials stay in server runtime configuration.

Decide whether first sign-in creates an account and whether existing accounts may be linked. Identify people with a stable provider identity, not matching names or emails alone. Identity integration and business permission assignment remain separate.

## Corporate sign-in example

Organizations with a central identity platform can reuse company accounts to reduce duplicate accounts and passwords. Configure business permissions separately after connecting identity.

```text
Connect Northstar's existing corporate identity provider using OIDC.
Keep password sign-in and add a Corporate sign-in button to the branded page.
Employees visit the company identity provider and sign in with their company account.
Show consent explaining the basic identity and email requested by the transport application.
Return to the workspace after consent; canceling must not sign the employee into the application.
Allow account creation at first sign-in, identified by the provider's stable user identity.
Do not merge accounts by matching names or emails, or grant new accounts administrator access.
List the information the provider administrator must supply, the callback to register, and application configuration.
```

### 1. Open company sign-in

Choose **Continue with Company account** on the transport application’s sign-in page. Password sign-in remains available.

![Company sign-in entry in the transport application](../assets/northstar-company-entry-en.png)

### 2. Authenticate with the company identity provider

The browser redirects to the independent **Northstar Identity** service. Enter the company username and password, then click **Sign in**. The transport application does not collect the company password on its own page.

![Sign in at the company identity provider](../assets/northstar-company-login-en.png)

### 3. Authorize the transport application

After authentication, **Authorize Northstar Logistics** shows the signed-in employee, Dana Reed, and the requested information: employee identifier, name, and email.

Choose **Allow access** to continue, or **Cancel** to stop authorization.

![Company identity and requested access on the consent page](../assets/northstar-company-consent-en.png)

### 4. Return to the workspace

Authorization redirects back to the transport application. Open the avatar menu to see **Dana Reed** and the company email. The application has established its own signed-in session.

![Return to the workspace with Dana Reed’s identity](../assets/northstar-company-signed-in-en.png)

Creating an account on first sign-in does not grant order access or administrator permissions. This new account has no business data permissions yet, so its workspace shows no orders. Administrators can assign appropriate [Permission sets](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/authorization/permission-sets.md).

Company sign-in establishes identity; the application’s business permissions govern pages, orders, and actions. Whether consent is shown or remembered depends on the company identity provider’s configuration.

## Other integration needs

For GitHub or Google, specify whether to keep passwords and how to create and link accounts, and ask the Agent for provider application and callback preparation.

For an internal ticket protocol:

```text
The company portal redirects to Northstar with a single-use ticket.
Follow the supplied protocol to verify it and use the returned stable identity to locate an existing application account.
Do not automatically create accounts; explain how to request access when none is found.
Keep password sign-in and enter the transport workspace after success.
```

Also specify whether sign-out leaves the identity provider, how existing employees link accounts, and role-specific landing pages. The integration includes any required binding pages, authentication extensions, and data structures.

## Verify the result

- Password sign-in remains available and company sign-in redirects to the identity provider.
- Allowing access returns the correct identity; cancelling does not sign in.
- Repeated sign-in does not duplicate or incorrectly merge accounts; new accounts receive no automatic administrator permissions.

Return to the [related overview scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#sso) to adapt the prompt and continue with your Agent.

# Protecting pages and APIs

[← Authentication overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md) · [Open the related scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#protect)

Northstar can publish its transport service information while keeping customer records, orders, and its workspace internal. Authentication establishes whether a caller is signed in; authorization determines access afterward.

> The /main/services, /main/orders, and /main/api/northstar paths belong to this example. Ask the Agent to use your application’s actual routes, APIs, and base path.

[Public information and internal work](#public-information-and-internal-work) · [Use the current employee identity](#use-the-current-employee-identity) · [Page and API requirements](#page-and-api-requirements) · [Account lifecycle and deployment](#account-lifecycle-and-deployment)

## Public information and internal work

An application can include public pages and internal work. Visitors can browse public content without sign-in; protected records require authentication and authorization.

```text
Add a public transport services page for Northstar without requiring registration or sign-in.
Use Northstar’s blue brand style to introduce its Yangtze River Delta network, regional transport, business delivery, and shipment coordination.
Show a contact email and an Employee orders entry. Signed-in employees can visit the public page too.
Its public reading API must not return internal orders or customer records.
Keep authentication and business permissions on the workspace, customer and order pages, and their APIs.
Direct anonymous visitors to sign-in when they open internal pages.
```

### Browse company information without signing in

Open `/main/services` to browse Northstar’s public service page directly. Visitors can see the Shanghai, Hangzhou, and Suzhou service network and the three service areas without registering or signing in. Internal customer and order records are not shown.

![Public Northstar service information without sign-in](../assets/northstar-public-services-en.png)

The business prompt above produces this page. Branding, layout, and service information can follow the company’s needs.

### Require sign-in for employee orders

Choose **Open employee orders** to visit the internal `/main/orders` address. Anonymous visitors are redirected to sign-in. After signing in, business permissions determine their order access.

Entering the internal order URL directly also leads to sign-in. Knowing the address does not grant business access.

![Opening employee orders anonymously redirects to sign-in](../assets/northstar-internal-orders-login-en.png)

Compare these example addresses:

| Address                                | Anonymous result                              |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `http://localhost:13200/main/services` | Displays public transport service information |
| `http://localhost:13200/main/orders`   | Redirects to application sign-in              |

### Protect pages and APIs separately

The public page reads company information from `GET /main/api/public/company`. This separate endpoint returns only the company name, service regions, service entries, and contact email. It does not query or return internal customers, employees, or orders.

Internal APIs still require authentication. An anonymous call to `GET /main/api/northstar` returns **401** without order data. Browsers visiting internal pages are redirected to sign-in; scripts calling protected APIs receive an authentication error and must provide valid identity.

Pages and APIs declare their own access requirements. Hidden navigation and browser checks cannot replace server protection.

## Use the current employee identity

Use the current authenticated identity when records need actor traceability. Record it on the server rather than relying on manually supplied identities.

```text
When creating an order, obtain the acting employee from the server-side session and record them.
Do not ask employees to supply or impersonate another acting user.
Assign an order owner separately under business rules; do not confuse ownership with creation.
```

Order owner, creator, and assigned driver are distinct fields. Authentication provides the current identity; business rules define fields and access scopes.

## Page and API requirements

| Scenario                      | Page behavior                    | API requirement                          |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Transport service information | Public and signed-in access      | Public content; optional identity        |
| Workspace, customers, orders  | Anonymous visitors enter sign-in | Authentication plus business permissions |
| Sign-in and password recovery | Guest-facing                     | Corresponding authentication flow        |
| Order-reading scripts         | No browser page required         | API key and owner permissions            |

Missing identity on a protected API returns 401; missing permission after authentication returns 403. API keys do not bypass authorization.

## Account lifecycle and deployment

Disable accounts and revoke sessions when employees leave or access is paused. An HR integration that performs those operations also requires authentication and authorization.

Deployment configuration covers application secrets, public address and path, cookies, and shared storage for multiple instances. Provider callbacks and password reset links must match the actual access address. Reverse proxies must forward protocol, Host, and cookies correctly.

Give the Agent these access requirements to implement page and API protection with the application’s authentication and authorization capabilities.

## Verify the result

- Visitors can read public information without receiving internal records.
- Internal pages redirect unauthenticated visitors to sign-in.
- Internal APIs enforce identity and business authorization on the server.

Return to the [related overview scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#protect) to adapt the prompt and continue with your Agent.



---
url: /capabilities/auth/login-pages.md
---

# Customizing sign-in pages

[← Authentication overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md) · [Open the related scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#brand)

After setting up accounts and the required authentication methods, customize the sign-in page for your company.

The sign-in page belongs to the application source. Its name, logo, copy, imagery, layout, and colors can follow a company brand while preserving authentication, error feedback, and password recovery.

> Customize application-owned branding, layout, and text while preserving the existing authentication actions, error handling, account rules, and recovery flows.

[Example: Northstar employee sign-in](#example-northstar-employee-sign-in) · [View the result](#view-the-result) · [Further customization](#further-customization)

## Example: Northstar employee sign-in

Northstar wants its employees to recognize the company and the purpose of the transport workspace. Accounts are managed centrally, without public registration.

```text
Customize the existing transport application's sign-in page for Northstar Logistics.

Use a pale-blue truck and mountain-road illustration, a white page panel, and a pale blue-gray grid backdrop for readable text.
Show the company name and icon at the top. Place a welcome message and transport dispatch, delivery tracking, and team collaboration copy on the left.
Place a white sign-in form on the right, with dark text, white inputs, and a blue sign-in button.
Preserve username or email and password sign-in, password visibility, error feedback, and password recovery.
Disable public registration on both the page and the server while retaining the registration page and components for future use.
Use consistent branding on sign-in and password recovery pages, with Chinese and English copy.
```

## View the result

The sign-in page uses a pale-blue mountain-road and truck illustration with company branding and transport business copy. Welcome copy appears on the left, and a white sign-in form sits on the right. Dark text and a blue button make the form easy to distinguish. Backgrounds, colors, and layouts can follow the company’s needs.

![Transport company sign-in with a pale-blue truck illustration and branded form](../assets/northstar-branded-login-en.png)

Page customization reuses existing forms and authentication actions. Hiding a registration link must be accompanied by disabling registration on the server.

## Further customization

Describe background images, form position, brand colors, fonts, or role-specific landing pages. Consider narrow screens and dark mode, and enforce business access on the server.

Password recovery requires an actual configured reset-email service. A visible link does not mean that service is ready.

## Verify the result

- The transport branding and form work on desktop and mobile.
- Password visibility, errors, and password recovery remain usable.
- Self-registration is disabled on the server, with reusable registration components retained.

Return to the [related overview scenario](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/auth/index.md#brand) to adapt the prompt and continue with your Agent.
