# Languages

Add interface and server translations, configure the default language, and preserve individual language choices.

Choose a scenario in the overview and adapt its prompt to your application. See the [usage guide](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/i18n/usage.md) for detailed instructions.



---
url: /capabilities/i18n/usage.md
---

# Language switching

A NocoBase 3 application supports multiple languages out of the box, with English and Chinese built in.

Switch between the built-in languages, or ask a Coding Agent to add a language or change the default.

## Switching the language

Open the account menu at the top right, choose **Language**, and pick one.

The switch takes effect immediately without a reload, and the interface a plugin contributes follows along.

The choice is stored in the current browser and survives a refresh, but does not sync to another device with the account. Switching to Chinese changes nothing for anyone else, and does not change the application's default language.

## Adding a language

Add interface and server-message translations when users need another language for the same business application. This example adds Spanish.

The languages an application offers come from its own locale files — **adding a locale file is adding a language**.

Those files live on both sides: `client/locales/` decides which languages appear in the switcher, and `server/locales/` decides which ones the server can answer in. Keeping the two aligned is recommended. A language available only on the client can still be selected: the interface switches, the server uses English, and an informational toast explains the fallback.

Tell a Coding Agent which language to support and where to use it. For example:

```text
Add Spanish to my application. Translate the interface and server messages, and add Spanish to the language menu.
```

It creates the locale files, registers them in the loader map, and checks that both sides agree. Refresh the page afterwards and the switcher has a new entry.

If a language ended up on only one side, this command reports it:

```bash
pnpm nocobase locales check
```

## Setting the default language

The default language is what **someone who has never chosen one** sees the first time they open the application. Set it in `config.yml`:

```yaml
i18n:
  defaultLocale: zh-CN
```

It is `en-US` when unset. Refresh the page after the updated configuration takes effect.

In both development and production, the server sets the HTML `lang` attribute to this default before sending the page. The client then synchronizes `lang` and text direction with its resolved language, including a previously saved choice, and keeps them updated when the language changes. Changing the deployment's default language does not require rebuilding the client.

:::tip Anyone who has already chosen is unaffected

The default applies only to a browser that has made no choice. If you change this setting and your own interface stays as it was, you most likely switched language by hand at some point — try another browser, or clear the site data.

:::

The default language has a second job: text with no translation in the language in use falls back to it.

## Languages a plugin has

A plugin has not necessarily translated every language your application offers. What it has not translated falls back in this order:

```text
the language in use  →  the application's default  →  English
```

For example: the application defaults to Chinese, you added Spanish, and a plugin translated only Chinese and English. A Spanish-speaking user sees your own text in Spanish and that plugin's text in Chinese.

To put a plugin's wording in your own words, ask a Coding Agent to follow the application's internationalization guidance and override it in your application's locale files.

## Common questions

### I switched language, but part of the interface is still English

That text may not have a translation in the selected language. It falls back to the application default, then English. Ask a Coding Agent to add the application translation or override the corresponding plugin text.

### I added a locale file, but the switcher does not list it

Check that you added it under `client/locales/` — that is the side the switcher reads. Then run `pnpm nocobase locales check` to see whether both sides agree. A new locale file also needs the dev server restarted.

### The interface switched, but what the server returns is still in the old language

Usually the language was added to `client/locales/` alone. Without the corresponding server translations, the server falls back to English. Ask a Coding Agent to add the language file under `server/locales/`.

### Two tabs on the same account affect each other

The server stores the language on the session, and tabs sharing an account share one session, so the later switch overwrites the earlier. The interface itself is unaffected — each tab shows its own language. What is affected is what the server produces, such as error messages. This is a known limitation.

## Northstar example

Dispatch staff can switch the same workspace to Chinese while overseas colleagues use English. Customer names, destinations, and other business values remain unchanged.

![The same transport workspace in Chinese](.././assets/northstar-workspace-cn.png)

**The same business interface can switch to Chinese without changing its records.**

# Themes

Adjust colors, typography, and density while preserving clear, usable light and dark appearances.

Choose a scenario in the overview and adapt its prompt to your application. See the [usage guide](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/theme/usage.md) for detailed instructions.



---
url: /capabilities/theme/usage.md
---

# Themes

NocoBase 3 themes control colors, fonts, text sizes, spacing, corners, and shadows. **Theme code lives in your application project**, so you can customize it directly without installing a plugin.

Use a built-in theme, or describe the appearance you want to a Coding Agent. For example, match your organization's brand colors or make tables and forms more compact.

## Built-in themes

Two themes are included:

| Theme   | Appearance                                                                                                                 |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Default | Neutral colors with standard spacing and rounded corners                                                                   |
| Compact | The same colors as Default, with reduced spacing, some text line heights, and corner radii for greater information density |

In the **Appearance** panel, choose a theme and a color mode: **Light**, **Dark**, or **System**. Theme and color mode are independent choices. Both built-in themes support light and dark modes.

Your theme choice is saved in the current browser and restored after a refresh. It does not sync to other devices with your account. Choosing a theme changes the appearance in your browser; editing its code changes the appearance for everyone using that theme.

## Editing a theme

If a theme is close to what you need, ask a Coding Agent to adjust it. Specify which theme to change, the desired changes, and what to keep.

For example, keep the compact layout and change the primary color to blue:

```text
Update the Compact theme: use blue as the primary color and slightly increase the corner radius. Keep the current fonts, text sizes, and compact spacing.
```

You can include brand color values, font requirements, or reference screenshots. For example, specify `#2563EB` as the primary color or provide a screenshot showing the desired corners and shadows.

To change only the name, ask: “Rename Compact to High Density. Keep its appearance and update the name in all supported languages.”

## Adding a theme

To keep existing themes and add another appearance, ask a Coding Agent to create a theme. Describe its name, style, and purpose, and which existing theme to use as a starting point.

For example:

```text
Create a Forest theme with green as the primary color, soft backgrounds, moderately rounded corners, and subtle shadows.
```

The Coding Agent creates the theme, adds it to the available choices, and configures its name. Select it in **Appearance**.

## Removing a theme

Remove retired themes from appearance options and let existing selections fall back to the application default.

Tell the Coding Agent which theme to remove. Browsers that previously selected it will use the application's default theme.

```text
Remove the Forest theme.
```

When removing the application's current default theme, specify another theme as the default for first-time visits and when a previously selected theme is unavailable.

## Viewing the result

After the changes, select the theme in **Appearance** to view its colors, fonts, and layout. Switch between light and dark modes to see how the theme looks in each.

Images, embedded pages, and some third-party components need separate adjustments. Include them in your request if they should use the same colors or style.

## Developer reference

To edit theme code directly, refer to these files. Paths are relative to the application project root and use the default application template as an example.

| File                                 | Purpose                     | Used for                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `client/theme/themes/default.css`    | Spacious theme appearance   | Editing Default                            |
| `client/theme/themes/compact.css`    | Compact theme appearance    | Editing or removing Compact                |
| `client/theme/themes/<theme-id>.css` | Custom theme appearance     | Adding, editing, or removing custom themes |
| `client/theme/theme-presets.ts`      | Theme choices in Appearance | Adding or removing themes                  |
| `client/styles.css`                  | Loading theme styles        | Adding or removing themes                  |
| `client/locales/zh-CN.ts`            | Chinese theme names         | Adding, removing, or renaming themes       |
| `client/locales/en-US.ts`            | English theme names         | Adding, removing, or renaming themes       |

Editing a theme's appearance usually requires changes only to its theme file. Adding or removing a theme also involves the theme list, style imports, and locale files. Additional languages or new fonts may require corresponding translations or font assets.

## Northstar brand theme

```text
Add a Northstar theme based on Compact. Use a deep blue primary color, retain its fonts and density, and slightly increase the corner radius. Support light and dark modes. Keep the existing presets and translate the new name into Chinese and English.
```

![Northstar appearance options](.././assets/northstar-appearance-en.png)

**Users can choose a theme and light, dark or system color mode.**

![Northstar brand in light mode](.././assets/northstar-brand-light-en.png)

**The brand theme displays the same business in light mode.**

![Northstar brand in dark mode](.././assets/northstar-brand-dark-en.png)

**Switching to dark mode retains business data and actions.**

# Notifications

Send in-app messages or email when business events occur, with useful links and traceable delivery results.

Choose a scenario in the overview and adapt its prompt to your application. See the [usage guide](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/notification/usage.md) for detailed instructions.



---
url: /capabilities/notification/usage.md
---

# Notifications

Notifications support **four channel categories: in-app messages, email, Feishu group robots and DingTalk group robots**. Email supports **SMTP and Resend**. A business event can use several channels, with an independent delivery result for each.

| Channel               | Supported integration      | Use                                                   |
| --------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| In-app messages       | Application message center | Notify application users and link to related records. |
| Email                 | SMTP or Resend             | Send notifications to recipients' email addresses.    |
| Feishu group robots   | Group robot webhook        | Send business messages to a Feishu group.             |
| DingTalk group robots | Group robot webhook        | Send business messages to a DingTalk group.           |

The application selects when to notify, the recipients, content and destination page. Notification services handle delivery, delivery records and retry history. Other notification services can also be added through extensions.

## Example: send an in-app notification

Use in-app messages to send business reminders to application users. This example notifies the operator of transport progress and links to the order detail.

```text
Add Send progress update to Northstar transport orders. Send an in-app notification with the current status to the current operator's message center. Include the order number, origin, destination, and status, with a link to the order detail. Notify the same recipient only once for each order version. Do not change the transport state. Add a personal Message center and an administrator-only Notification log.
```

Open NS-2026-003, select **Send progress update**, then open **Message center**. This example sends the message to the demo operator, showing Suzhou → Nanjing and the completed status.

![Real transport progress notification](.././assets/northstar-notification-en.png)

**The message center shows the progress reminder and a link to its order.**

Select the message title to open its order. Messages persist across refreshes and support read, unread, and removal actions. A message does not grant additional access to the referenced order.

## Trigger from business processes

Notify the actual applicant when approval or other business work produces a result, with a link to its details.

Once actual applicants and approval results exist, ask the Agent to notify only the applicant after approval or rejection, include the order and result, and link to the application. Pending applications should produce no result notification, and each result should notify once. A notification failure must not reverse the saved business result. User identities and decisions must come from the business process. See [Approvals](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/approval/index.md).

## Review notification logs

Notification services provide delivery logs and query APIs. An application can build a page for its administrators. **The Agent built this example's Notification log page for the transport application, using actual delivery records.**

Administrators open **Notification log** to review transport updates and dispatch digests, with source, reference, channels, status, attempts, and time.

![Real notification delivery records](.././assets/northstar-notification-logs-en.png)

**Administrators can inspect notification channels, processing status and attempts.**

`completed` describes processing of the notification's deliveries; provider acceptance and a recipient reading a message are different facts. Channels are independent. If no message arrives, first check whether the business generated a record, then inspect its delivery, recipient, and configuration.

To check a channel, ask the Agent to add a **Send test notification** entry. Select a configured channel and recipient, send the message, then inspect its delivery record.

## Email and group channels

Reach users outside the application through email or group channels. Track each channel independently to follow delivery and handle failures.

| Channel            | Preparation                                                                  | Configuration                           |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| SMTP               | Server, port, sender account, password or authorization code, sender address | `notification.channels` in `config.yml` |
| Resend             | API key and authorized sender                                                | Same                                    |
| Feishu or DingTalk | Group robot webhook and optional signing secret                              | Same                                    |
| In-app             | Actual application user ID                                                   | Existing in-app channel                 |

Keep credentials on the server. Ask the Agent to add approval-result email alongside in-app notifications, resolve the actual applicant's email, skip email when absent, preserve each channel's independent result, and show delivery logs without exposing credentials. Use a stable identifier per logical notification. Inspect uncertain external delivery before sending again; retry and compensation follow the business scenario.

## Related capabilities

- [Scheduled tasks](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/scheduler.md)
- [Workflows](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/workflow/index.md)
- [Mail](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/index.md)

# Scheduled tasks

Describe what should run, when it should run, and who should receive the result. Inspect schedules and execution history.

Choose a scenario in the overview and adapt its prompt to your application. See the [usage guide](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/scheduler/usage.md) for detailed instructions.



---
url: /capabilities/scheduler/usage.md
---

# Scheduled tasks

NocoBase 3 can run business operations at specified times or intervals. For example, remind people to process pending work each day, generate a weekly report, or periodically synchronize business data.

Tell your Agent when to run, which data to process, and what result to produce. After the Agent integrates the business logic, administrators can view the schedule and execution records in Settings, and pause or resume the task.

## Before you start

This example adds approval reminders to an existing order application. Prepare pending orders and coordinator accounts, and specify who reviews each order.

Tell the Agent the execution time and timezone, which orders to include, who receives the notification, and where it opens when clicked.

## Example: remind coordinators about pending orders

Reviewers need to process pending orders promptly. On weekdays, the application checks pending orders, groups them by coordinator, and sends an in-app reminder.

```text
Add a Awaiting dispatch reminder to the existing order application.

At 09:00 Beijing time every weekday, find orders awaiting approval, group them by coordinator, and send each coordinator one in-app notification.
Include the pending order count and link to the pending order list. Send nothing when there are no pending orders.
Administrators can view the schedule and execution records in Settings, and pause or resume reminders.
```

### Viewing the result

1. As an administrator, open **Automation**. **Awaiting dispatch reminder** shows the schedule, timezone, next trigger, and current status.

2. Click the task name to open its details. **Execution records** shows each execution's time, duration, and status. **Succeeded** in this example means the reminder task ran successfully.

3. As a coordinator, open the notification center to see the pending order count. Click the notification to open the pending order list and process approvals.

The schedule determines when to run. Finding orders, counting them, and sending the notification are business operations integrated by the Agent. See [Notifications](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/notification.md) for notification capabilities.

## Managing tasks

### Pausing and resuming

Administrators can use the switch in the task list or details. Pausing prevents new scheduled triggers; resuming continues according to the configured schedule. Historical records remain available, and business work that has already started continues under its executor.

### Changing the time or business rules

Adjust an existing scheduled task to a new work schedule while retaining its records, recipients and business content.

Ask the Agent to update the existing task. For example:

```text
Change Awaiting dispatch reminder to run at 10:00 Beijing time every weekday.
Keep the existing order selection, recipients, and notification content.
```

After the change, check the updated schedule and next trigger in the details. The Agent adds, edits, or removes task definitions in application code; administrators view and enable or disable tasks in Settings.

## Further use

### Generating reports

Generate reports on a fixed schedule and notify responsible users instead of relying on manual reminders.

Add a schedule and result notification to an existing reporting capability:

```text
At 08:00 Beijing time every Monday, generate last week's sales summary and notify the sales manager.
Include sales revenue, order count, and regional totals. Administrators can view the task and execution records.
```

### Synchronizing data

Periodically synchronize selected fields maintained in an external system to keep the application current without duplicate maintenance.

For an existing integration, specify the interval and data to process:

```text
Every 10 minutes, synchronize customer statuses from the existing customer system into the matching application records.
Keep other customer information unchanged. Administrators can view the schedule and execution records.
```

## Common questions

### Why does the task run at a different time than expected?

Check its timezone in the details. Specify Beijing time or your business timezone in the request; this example uses `Asia/Shanghai`. After the Agent changes the time, check the next trigger.

### Where can I see the business result?

View execution records in the task details and results in the relevant business page. This example uses the coordinator's inbox and pending order list; reporting tasks produce reports, and synchronization tasks update business data.

### Does the task run while the application is stopped?

Tasks require a running application process. For continuous operation, deployment administrators keep the service running. Multi-instance deployments also need a shared scheduling backend.

## Developer reference

Application code owns task definitions and execution targets. These are the main integration points:

| Integration point                             | Purpose                                         |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `schedulerServiceToken`                       | Resolve the scheduler service                   |
| `registerTarget()`                            | Register the business execution target          |
| `defineSchedule()`                            | Define the name, schedule, timezone, and target |
| Application Provider `register()` or `boot()` | Register targets and schedule definitions       |

Use a stable `key` unique within the application. Schedules support five- or six-field Cron expressions and IANA timezone names; the default timezone is `UTC`. Short tasks can complete directly. Longer tasks can use the application's background execution service and report their final outcome.

Application startup synchronizes definitions while preserving administrator enable/disable choices. Developers can also synchronize from the application root:

```bash
pnpm nocobase scheduler sync --json
```

After removing old task definitions in a deployment, deployment administrators can run the following once the complete code and plugin manifest is loaded:

```bash
node dist/cli/index.js scheduler sync --finalize --json
```

This deactivates tasks removed from code and preserves their history. A single process can use the built-in memory backend. Multi-instance deployments use a shared Redis backend, selected through `jobs.default`. Use `scheduler.jobs` for a separate scheduling configuration and keep its `attempts` at `1`.

## Northstar result

The demo administrator receives a digest of orders awaiting dispatch. The list shows the weekday 09:00 Asia/Shanghai schedule and a real succeeded execution; the message links back to the order list. Notification delivery remains independently observable.

![Real schedule and execution](.././assets/northstar-scheduler-en.png)

**The task page retains its schedule and this successful run.**

![Real dispatch reminder](.././assets/northstar-scheduler-notice-en.png)

**The awaiting-dispatch digest reached the demonstration account’s message center.**

This example first ran once with a short interval, then restored the weekday 09:00 schedule. The execution shown belongs to that demonstration; the next run follows the restored configuration.

# Mail

Mail lets users connect their own mailboxes, synchronize incoming messages, read messages and attachments, and compose or reply without leaving the application. It supports sales communication, customer service, and project collaboration.

## Available capabilities

| Capability            | Purpose                                                                         |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Connect mailboxes     | Connect through IMAP/SMTP or authorize Gmail and Microsoft 365 accounts.        |
| Synchronize and read  | Import messages from a chosen starting date and view messages and attachments.  |
| Compose and reply     | Write, reply, or forward with attachments, signatures, and templates.           |
| Organize messages     | Search, mark as read, star, and label messages, depending on the provider.      |
| Connect business data | Add mail actions to customer or project pages and include business information. |

Mail is for correspondence between users and external contacts. For approval results and automatic system reminders, see [Notifications](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/notification.md).

## Use Mail

- [Mailbox Configuration](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/configuration.md): what administrators and mailbox users need to prepare.
- [Sync and Send Email](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/quick-start.md): add a mail center, read customer inquiries, and reply.
- [More Mail Features](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/usage.md): use signatures and templates and connect business pages.
- [Developer Reference](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/development.md): integrate pages, permissions, and background jobs.

IMAP/SMTP supports receiving new messages and sending email. Read, delete, and move changes made in other clients are not fully synchronized. Consider Gmail or Microsoft 365 when you need more complete mailbox organization.



---
url: /capabilities/mail/quick-start.md
---

# Sync and Send Email

This example adds a mail center where a sales representative reads and replies to a customer quotation request. The message list, reading view, and reply actions share one workspace.

## Before you start

- An administrator configures an available mail provider. See [Mailbox Configuration](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/configuration.md).
- Users prepare their mailbox credentials or app password. Gmail and Microsoft 365 use provider authorization.

## Example: reply to customer email

Connect mailboxes when employees need to read and reply to customer messages within the application. Preserve subjects, content and context while reducing system switches.

Give the following prompt to your Agent:

```text
Add a mail center and a mailbox account management entry to the application. Users can connect their own mailboxes, select a mailbox, synchronize incoming messages, read messages and attachments, and reply.

When a sales representative receives a quotation request, they can reply from the mail center. Keep the original subject and conversation context, and address the reply to the original sender. Each user works with their own connected mailboxes.
```

### 1. Connect a mailbox

Open the mailbox accounts page and click **Connect account**. Select a provider, enter the mailbox information, and choose a starting date for the initial synchronization. This example uses a dedicated sales mailbox. Its address and connection status appear in the account list.

### 2. Synchronize and read incoming messages

Open the mail center, select the sales mailbox, and synchronize incoming messages. The list contains quotation requests, delivery arrangements, and information requests. Select a message to read it.

### 3. Reply to the customer

Click **Reply** and enter the pricing and delivery details. The reply includes the recipient, subject, and original context. Click **Send** when ready.

### 4. View the received reply

The customer mailbox receives the pricing and delivery information. Both parties can continue the same conversation.

For signatures, templates, and business page integration, see [More Mail Features](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/usage.md).

## Northstar example

The new application synchronizes the dedicated demo mailboxes and displays their existing fleet-business conversation, reply editor, and received quotation. No new external message is required to reproduce these screenshots.

![Connected demo mailboxes](../assets/northstar-mail-accounts-en.png)

**Personal mailboxes are connected and their connection status is visible.**

![Fleet-business correspondence](../assets/northstar-mail-reading-en.png)

**Users can read synchronized messages and their content in the application.**

![Reply editor](../assets/northstar-mail-reply-en.png)

**The reply editor retains context and lets users compose their response.**

![Previously received demo reply](../assets/northstar-mail-received-en.png)

**The customer mailbox displays the quotation reply in the existing demonstration conversation.**

# More Mail Features

Mail provides signatures, templates, message reading, and a composer. Applications can place these capabilities on account pages, customer details, or order details.

Northstar provides **Mailbox accounts** and **Customer communication** navigation entries and embeds mail actions in customer and transport order details. Ask the Agent:

```text
Add Mailbox accounts and Customer communication to the application navigation.
Embed NocoBase's account management page for mailbox connections, signatures, and templates.
Embed the mail workspace for employees to read and send through their own connected mailboxes.
```

See [Configure Mail](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/configuration.md) for connections and [Developer Reference](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/development.md) for integration.

## Use mail signatures

Save recurring team names, job titles, and contact details as signatures to avoid entering them each time. Signatures belong to a mailbox account and can have a default.

```text
Prepare a Northstar Operations signature for the business mailbox,
including Northstar Logistics, Operations team, and transport coordination details.
Let employees manage signatures from Mailbox accounts and select them when composing.
```

Open **Mailbox accounts → Signatures**, select an account, enter the signature name and content, and save. Set the frequently used signature as the default.

![Manage mailbox signatures](../assets/northstar-mail-signatures-en.png)

**The business mailbox has a saved default signature, available when composing.**

## Use mail templates

Save recurring subjects and message content as templates. Templates belong to the current user. An application can also supply the current business record to populate variables such as customer names and order numbers.

```text
Prepare a Transport progress update template with the order number in the subject
and customer name, origin, destination, transport status, and expected delivery in the body.
Provide the current order and customer when opening the composer from order details.
Employees can apply the template, edit the content, and select an existing signature.
```

Open **Mailbox accounts → Templates** to manage subjects and content. This example uses variables such as `{{record.customer.name}}` and `{{record.order.number}}`.

![Manage the transport progress template](../assets/northstar-mail-templates-en.png)

Open the composer from transport order details, click **Template**, and select **Transport progress update**. Click **Signature** to select a signature.

![Apply the template and signature to an order email](../assets/northstar-mail-template-applied-en.png)

**The template populates the subject and body with customer and order information, followed by the signature. Everything remains editable before sending.**

:::info Important

The embedding business page must supply template variables. Saving a template does not automatically load customer or order data. Unmatched variables remain unchanged. Review recipients and content before sending.

:::

## Read correspondence on business pages

Embed mail lists and message reading in customer details to see communication while reviewing the customer's information. Match messages by contact email.

```text
Add Correspondence to customer details.
Match the customer's contact email against senders, recipients, and copied recipients.
Only show messages accessible through the current employee's own connected mailboxes.
Select a message to read its body. Reply opens the mail composer with its reply relationship retained.
The employee reviews the content before sending. Provide Refresh mail and Load more.
```

Open customer details and select a message under **Correspondence**. This example reads already synchronized messages using the mail reading component.

![Customer correspondence and message body](../assets/northstar-customer-mail-en.png)

**Customer information and related correspondence appear on the same page, without searching separately for the contact email.**

Click **Reply** to open the composer.

![Reply from customer details](../assets/northstar-customer-mail-reply-en.png)

**The reply composer populates recipients and the original subject. Employees can edit the message and select a signature or template.**

:::info Important

Enter the contact email accurately: it determines the correspondence match. Business record access and mailbox access are enforced separately. Access to a customer does not grant access to another employee's mailbox.

:::

## Compose from business pages

Populate contacts and record details when composing order progress updates to reduce copying and entry errors.

```text
Add Compose progress email to transport order details.
Read the recipient from the customer contact and include the order number in the subject.
Populate the body with the customer, origin, destination, and transport status.
Employees review and edit before sending through their connected mailbox.
Allow existing templates and signatures; do not send automatically.
```

Open transport order details and click **Compose progress email**.

![Order information in the mail composer](../assets/northstar-order-mail-en.png)

**Order information populates the subject and body, ready for editing before sending.**

## Usage tips

- Synchronize to retrieve new mail; refreshing displays messages already synchronized to the application.
- Choose the required history range for the initial synchronization.
- Organize mail with search, stars, and labels. Whether changes reach the provider depends on the integration.



---
url: /capabilities/mail/configuration.md
---

# Mailbox Configuration

Administrators configure how the application connects to a mail provider. Users then connect their own mailboxes. If a provider is already available, users can connect from the mailbox accounts page.

## Administrator preparation

Configure the provider’s mail servers and connection methods before connecting personal mailboxes. Users then connect accounts without repeating provider setup.

| Integration   | Information required                                                                         |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| IMAP/SMTP     | Incoming and outgoing server addresses, ports, and secure connection settings.               |
| Gmail         | A Google OAuth application, client information, and the application callback URL.            |
| Microsoft 365 | A Microsoft OAuth application, client information, and any required organizational approval. |

The application developer or deployment administrator maintains these settings under `mail.providers` in the server configuration. Users connect personal mailboxes from the application's mailbox accounts page.

For example, give these mailbox.org server settings to your Agent:

```text
Configure mailbox.org integration for the application:
- IMAP server: imap.mailbox.org, port 993, using SSL/TLS.
- SMTP server: smtp.mailbox.org, port 465, using SSL/TLS.
Add a mailbox accounts page where users enter their email address, username, and password and choose a starting date for initial synchronization.
```

For OAuth, administrators register the application's callback URL with the provider and complete any required permission approval.

## Connect your mailbox

Open the mailbox accounts page and click **Connect account**:

- **IMAP/SMTP**: select the provider and enter the address, username, and password or app password required by the provider.
- **Gmail or Microsoft 365**: select the provider, sign in, and authorize access on the provider's page.
- Choose the starting date for importing existing messages.

Enter mailbox passwords in the connection form. Administrators store OAuth secrets in deployment configuration.

## Integration differences

Gmail and Microsoft 365 offer more complete synchronization and organization. IMAP/SMTP primarily imports new messages and sends email. It does not fully synchronize read, delete, or move changes from other clients, and does not support provider drafts, sender aliases, push synchronization, or moves to provider folders. Local application drafts can still save unsent content.

## Common questions

### The application has no mailbox entry

Ask your Agent to integrate Mail and add the mail center and mailbox accounts page to application navigation.

### OAuth does not return to the application

Ask an administrator to check the registered callback URL against the application configuration and ensure the return page is accessible.

### No messages appear after connection

Check that the synchronization starting date includes the messages and that synchronization has completed. Importing a large history takes time. If background jobs are not running, an administrator can inspect synchronization records and application services.



---
url: /capabilities/mail/development.md
---

# Developer Reference

Mail can be a standalone workspace or part of customer and project pages. The application owns page entries, provider configuration, and business associations. Mail provides account, sending, and synchronization capabilities.

## Integrate pages

`@nocobase/app-plugin-mail/client` exports two complete page components:

| Component           | Purpose                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `MailWorkspacePage` | Message list, reading, composition, and replies.                   |
| `MailAccountsPage`  | Mailbox connection, account management, signatures, and templates. |

Mount pages in application routes and add navigation entries. For custom composition, use public components from `@nocobase/app-plugin-mail/client/components`.

A mail center page can reuse the workspace directly:

```tsx
export { MailWorkspacePage as default } from '@nocobase/app-plugin-mail/client';
```

## Connect business data

The application defines associations between messages and business records. For example, match customer correspondence by contact email, or populate a project template with project name and progress. Specify the matching fields, recipient source, and whether sending requires confirmation.

Use `useMailClient()` for client operations and `mailServiceToken` for the server service. Refer to the application's OpenAPI document for HTTP request and response contracts.

## Configure access

| Resource          | Purpose                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `mail.workspace`  | Personal mail workspace.                                                 |
| `mail.admin`      | Administrative account overview and sending and synchronization records. |
| `mail.management` | Cross-user mail management.                                              |

Personal account and message operations enforce account ownership. Grant the relevant permissions to application roles and declare access rules for business pages separately.

## Providers and background jobs

Register Mail on the server and client and include its configuration factory in application configuration. Maintain provider settings under `mail.providers`. Sending and synchronization use background jobs. Keep the executor running and use a shared job backend for multiple instances.

OAuth also requires a public callback URL and a return page. For IMAP/SMTP limits, see [Mailbox Configuration](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/configuration.md#integration-differences).

For signature, template, and business page prompts, see [More Mail Features](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/mail/usage.md).



---
url: /capabilities/ai-employee/index.md
---

# AI employees overview

An AI employee is an application assistant with a defined responsibility. It can use page context, query business data, call permitted actions following working instructions, and answer with company knowledge. Ask your development Agent to connect these capabilities and build the conversation and result views your users need.

## Available capabilities

| Capability | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Page context](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-employee/page-context.md) | Answer about the order, customer or form currently open. |
| [Business queries](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-employee/business-data.md) | Find records using natural language and link results to application pages. |
| [Business actions](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-employee/business-actions.md) | Connect business actions with server-side authorization and execution records. |
| [Responsibilities and working rules](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-employee/work-rules.md) | Define tasks, response style and permitted operations. |
| [Company knowledge](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/answers.md) | Find supporting material and link answers to readable sources. |

Conversations can appear on a dedicated page, in a business block or beside the current page.

## Prepare an AI employee

The application needs the Agents capability and an available model service. A development Agent can connect the model, instructions and business actions; a separate employee creation form is optional.

```text
Connect a Transport assistant to the Northstar application using my configured model service.
It explains orders, finds records awaiting dispatch and offers advice using transport procedures.
Connect order-reading actions within the current user's access scope. Start with queries; do not automatically change orders or send notifications.
Provide conversation entry points on order lists and details, with follow-up questions and links to returned orders.
```

Model services can use cloud providers or an available local service. Specify the endpoint, available models and credential configuration. Business actions enforce access on the server.

Start with [page context](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-employee/page-context.md), then [business queries](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-employee/business-data.md).



---
url: /capabilities/ai-employee/page-context.md
---

# Page context

Users often ask questions about the record they are handling. An application can provide its identifier and necessary context to an AI employee, so users can ask what to do next without copying the customer, route and status again.

## Example: an assistant beside order details

```text
Add a Transport assistant panel beside Northstar order details.
Associate the conversation with the current order and use authorized business actions to read its customer, route, cargo, status, owner and driver.
Summarize the order and explain the next action for its stage. Include the corresponding business entry point.
Update context when the order changes; do not reuse the previous order's information.
Use the existing blue theme and keep the order and conversation visible together.
```

## View the result

Open the assistant beside **NS-2026-001** and ask:

```text
Summarize this order. What should I do next?
```

Order details remain on the left. The conversation identifies the associated order and explains the next step for Awaiting dispatch, with an entry point for driver assignment.

![Order details and the Transport assistant shown together](../assets/northstar-ai-order-context-en.png)

**The conversation follows the current order and connects to its business actions.**

:::tip Important

Context helps interpret a question; the server controls access. An order identifier does not grant permission to read that order. Define permitted actions and confirmation requirements before connecting writes, messages or approvals.

:::



---
url: /capabilities/ai-employee/business-data.md
---

# Business queries

An AI employee can translate a natural-language question into an authorized business query, organize the records and provide page links. Connected reading actions supply current business data rather than only general advice.

## Example: find orders awaiting dispatch

```text
Connect order queries to Northstar's Transport assistant.
Let employees ask for orders awaiting dispatch or filter by customer, stage or route.
Respect the current user's data access. Return the order number, customer, route and owner as cards that open order details.
Explain when there are no matching orders in the user's scope. Continue follow-up questions with the selected order's context.
```

## View the result

Open the assistant on the order list and ask:

```text
Which orders are awaiting dispatch? Show their customers and routes.
```

The cards group the order number, customer, route and owner. **NS-2026-001, NS-2026-002 and NS-2026-007** are awaiting dispatch in this example; users can select an order to open its details.

![Awaiting dispatch orders presented as linked cards](../assets/northstar-ai-order-query-en.png)

**Query results connect to order pages so users can continue handling a record.**

## Extend queries to actions

Ask the development Agent to connect a specific action, such as assigning a driver, creating a follow-up or preparing a notification. Define its inputs, permissions, confirmation and where users see the result.

Queries, advice and writes are different operations. Advice alone does not change a record. A connected write should display its actual outcome and processing record.



---
url: /capabilities/ai-employee/business-actions.md
---

# Perform business actions

AI employees can call business actions connected by the application, turning natural-language requests into work such as assigning a driver, creating a follow-up record, or preparing a notification. The application defines allowed actions, required inputs, confirmation, and how results are displayed.

For data changes, an employee can present an operation plan before execution. Business actions still pass server-side permission checks, and reported results must match the actual records.

## Example: assign a driver after confirmation

A Northstar dispatcher wants to assign driver Li Ming to **NS-2026-001** in the order conversation. The transport assistant first summarizes the order, driver, and status change, leaving the record unchanged until confirmation. After confirmation, it assigns the driver and changes the order from Awaiting dispatch to Awaiting acceptance.

Describe the requirement to your development Agent:

```text
Connect a driver-assignment action to Northstar's transport assistant.
Use the current order context and check user permissions, order status, and driver availability.
Show the order number, driver, and status change before writing; require user confirmation.
After confirmation, execute and show the actual order and operation record. Explain failures without reporting success.
```

## See the result

In the NS-2026-001 conversation, enter:

```text
Prepare to assign driver Li Ming to this order. Ask me to confirm first.
```

Review the plan and reply “Confirm execution.” The illustrated result shows Li Ming as the driver, Awaiting acceptance as the status, and Alice as the person who confirmed the completed operation.

![The transport assistant presents a plan and shows the driver assignment after confirmation](../assets/northstar-ai-business-actions-en.png)

**Confirmation in the conversation becomes a business record change that users can verify in the order and operation record.**

:::tip Important

Driver assignment requires an action provided by the application. Instructions or a prompt do not grant write access, and confirmation cannot bypass permissions, driver availability, or order-state checks. Assignment does not mean the driver has accepted the order and does not automatically send a notification.

:::



---
url: /capabilities/ai-employee/work-rules.md
---

# Responsibilities and work rules

An AI employee's instructions can define who it serves, its tasks, response priorities, and work rules. Work methods can be included in these instructions. Runtime modes that support skills can also reuse them, allowing different assistants to approach the same business question according to their responsibilities.

Instructions and skills guide how work is done. Application actions and permissions determine what can be executed. An employee's additional instructions cannot override application rules or the current task.

## Example: transport and customer assistants

Northstar wants its transport assistant to focus on orders and dispatch, and its customer assistant to focus on communication and follow-up. Asked what to prepare next for **NS-2026-001**, one organizes dispatch work and the other prepares customer communication. Order changes and message sending require confirmation according to application rules.

Describe the requirement to your development Agent:

```text
Prepare transport and customer assistants for Northstar using an existing available model service.
The transport assistant handles orders and dispatch, checking the route, delivery time, and drivers first. Require confirmation before changing orders.
The customer assistant handles communication and follow-up, preparing a delivery-message draft without taking over dispatch or sending automatically.
Connect reads and actions appropriate to each responsibility. Explain missing information rather than inventing conclusions.
Show the active assistant and associated order in conversations so their priorities are clear.
```

## See the result

Ask each assistant:

```text
What should we prepare next for this order?
```

The transport assistant lists route checks, driver lookup, and an assignment plan. The customer assistant lists contact checks, drafting a message, and waiting for confirmation before sending.

![Transport and customer assistants answer for the same order according to their responsibilities](../assets/northstar-ai-work-rules-en.png)

**The same question produces preparation for different responsibilities, showing employees who handles each task and where confirmation is needed.**

:::tip Important

Instructions do not replace access control. An assistant limited to preparing drafts should not receive sending actions. For actual operations, define inputs, permissions, confirmation, and result records together. Methods in skills should follow the same rules.

:::



---
url: /capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/index.md
---

# AI knowledge bases overview

A knowledge base organizes articles, files and business instructions into maintainable, searchable company material. Employees can read it directly or have an AI employee retrieve accessible content to support an answer.

## Available capabilities

| Capability | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Organize and import material](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/organize.md) | Spaces, folders, articles and files for different purposes. |
| [Read and search](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/search.md) | Read source material, find content and connect semantic retrieval as needed. |
| [Knowledge-based answers](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/answers.md) | Use company material in answers and link to sources. |
| [Access and collaboration](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/access.md) | Assign read, propose, edit and manage permissions. |
| [Versions and processing status](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/maintenance.md) | Keep versions and view file parsing and indexing status. |

The application composes the knowledge center's layout and entry points. Permissions, history and editing belong beside the relevant material rather than requiring a shared settings page.

## Use knowledge in your business

Northstar's material includes delivery requirements, temperature deviations and customer service procedures. Operations maintains the procedures, dispatchers read them, and the assistant answers questions with source links.

```text
Connect a knowledge center to Northstar for transport procedures, customer service material and driver handbooks.
Provide folders, articles, files, reading and search, with role-based access.
Let the Transport assistant answer from transport procedures and return document and passage links.
Connect the required model service, retrieval method and index while keeping sources clear in the employee interface.
```

Start with [knowledge-based answers](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/answers.md). Basic reading and maintenance can be used independently. AI answers require an available model; semantic retrieval also requires its model and index integration.



---
url: /capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/organize.md
---

# Organize and import materials

A knowledge base separates materials by space and organizes articles and files in folders. Articles suit business guidance that needs regular maintenance; files let you import existing materials. Uploaded files provide an original-file preview and extracted text for reading and search.

## Example: transport standards and driver manuals

Northstar's operations team maintains temperature-controlled transport and delivery requirements, and needs to make an existing pre-departure checklist available to drivers. Separate spaces help employees find materials by purpose.

Give the requirement to an Agent:

```text
Organize two knowledge spaces in Northstar's knowledge center:
Transport standards and Driver manuals.
Under Transport standards, create a Temperature-controlled transport folder
with Temperature-controlled transport standards and Delivery confirmation articles.
The standards article should cover Before departure, Handling temperature deviations,
and Delivery evidence.
Under Driver manuals, create a Pre-departure preparation folder with a file upload entry.
I will upload the existing Pre-departure checklist.pdf; do not invent its contents.
Employees can open articles or files from the tree.
Editors can create articles and folders and upload files.
```

![Knowledge spaces, folders, articles, and a completed file upload](../assets/northstar-knowledge-organize-en.png)

**Transport standards and driver manuals form a clear directory. Articles can be maintained directly, and existing PDFs can be placed in the appropriate folder for employees to read.**

:::tip Important

Maintaining materials requires editing permission. A successful upload and completed text extraction are separate states; confirm extraction has completed before searching file content. Organization and original-text reading work independently; semantic search requires a model and an index.

:::



---
url: /capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/search.md
---

# Read and search

Employees can open articles or files from the knowledge tree to read original business guidance, or enter keywords to find relevant materials. Search results show document titles, sections, and excerpts so users can judge relevance and return to the original context.

Once the application connects semantic search, employees can describe their question in natural language and find related passages by meaning without knowing the exact wording.

## Example: finding temperature-deviation requirements

A Northstar driver needs to find the handling requirements for a temperature deviation and verify the original text. They can search for “temperature deviation” when they know the terminology, or ask “What should a driver do when the cargo temperature is abnormal?” when they do not.

Give the requirement to an Agent:

```text
Provide reading and search entries in Northstar's knowledge center.
Employees can search for "temperature deviation", see documents, sections
and excerpts, and open the original text.
Connect semantic search so "What should a driver do when the cargo temperature
is abnormal?" also finds Handling temperature deviations in the transport standards.
Show the source of each result and open the original text when selected.
Keep the current user's readable materials as the search scope.
Confirm the required model and index are available;
do not treat keyword search as enabled semantic search.
```

![Natural-language search results, sources, and the original handling requirements](../assets/northstar-knowledge-search-en.png)

**With semantic search connected, a natural-language question finds relevant guidance. The document, section, and original passage provide evidence employees can check.**

:::tip Important

Keyword lookup is available directly. Semantic search requires the application to connect an appropriate model and a usable materials index. Finding relevant materials does not mean AI has composed an answer. For answers based on those materials, see [Answer questions using knowledge](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/answers.md).

:::



---
url: /capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/answers.md
---

# Knowledge-based answers

Company rules often live in documents. An AI employee can find accessible material, organize an answer around the question and provide sources for users to check and read further.

## Example: find transport exception procedures

```text
Let Northstar's Transport assistant use the transport procedures space.
Retrieve relevant material before answering procedural questions. Include document and passage links.
Say when no supporting material was found; do not invent company rules.
Provide a conversation panel in the knowledge center with the original text visible beside the answer.
Respect the knowledge scopes available to the current user and assistant, including restricted finance material.
```

## View the result

Open **Temperature-controlled transport** in the knowledge center and ask:

```text
What should the driver do if the shipment temperature is outside the agreed range?
```

The document stays on the left. The answer organizes recording the time and temperature, checking equipment, informing dispatch and following customer instructions. A source card links to **Handling temperature deviations**.

![Transport procedure, assistant answer and source passage](../assets/northstar-ai-knowledge-answer-en.png)

**Answers connect to company material so users can check the applicable requirements.**

:::tip Important

Knowledge explains how to handle a situation; business queries supply current facts. Maintain current material and its access rules. Advice from a document does not automatically become an executed business action.

:::



---
url: /capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/access.md
---

# Access and collaboration

Knowledge spaces, folders, and documents can grant read, propose, edit, and manage access. Readers consult content, contributors propose changes, editors maintain content and review proposals, and managers can also change access. Documents can inherit access from their space or parent folder, or allow only specified members.

## Example: maintain transport guidelines together

Northstar's operations administrators manage the transport guidelines space, while operations editors maintain its content. Dispatchers need to read guidelines and propose changes for editors to review. Financial materials are available only to authorized members.

```text
Assign access and collaboration permissions by responsibility in Northstar's knowledge center.
Operations administrators can manage transport guidelines, operations editors can edit and review proposals, and dispatchers can read and propose changes.
Show permissions and proposals beside documents. Allow only specified members to access financial materials; exclude dispatchers.
```

## See the result

Open **Temperature-controlled transport guidelines** to see each role's access. Dispatcher Emma proposes adding temperature deviation recording requirements. An operations editor can accept or reject the proposal; a pending proposal does not change the document directly. Financial materials use access limited to specified members, so dispatchers cannot access their content.

![Role access, a change proposal, and restricted financial materials](../assets/northstar-knowledge-access.png)

**Employees read and collaborate within their responsibilities, changes go through review, and restricted content stays within its authorized audience.**

:::tip Important

Space managers retain management access even when a document is limited to specified members. AI knowledge use must also respect access. Permission to propose changes does not grant direct editing or proposal review.

:::



---
url: /capabilities/ai-knowledge-base/maintenance.md
---

# Versions and processing status

Article and file updates retain version history so you can inspect previous content and compare changes. Extracting text from an uploaded file and building an index for semantic retrieval are separate stages: parsing completion means text has been extracted, while indexing status describes processing of the current document's sections.

## Example: update temperature-controlled transport guidelines

Northstar's operations editor adds deviation recording requirements to the guidelines. An operations administrator needs to compare versions, inspect file parsing and semantic indexing progress, and identify materials whose indexing is unfinished.

```text
Show version history and comparisons for the temperature-controlled transport guidelines in Northstar's knowledge center.
In the transport guidelines space with semantic retrieval enabled, show file parsing status, section indexing progress, and materials with unfinished indexing separately.
Show reasons and a reindex action for indexing failures. Do not display one parsed file as proof that the entire knowledge base is searchable.
```

## See the result

Open the version history of **Temperature-controlled transport guidelines.docx** and compare v2 with the current v3. The update adds requirements to record the time, temperature, and handling of deviations. File parsing is complete, but only **2 of 3 sections** have been indexed, with one still waiting. The unfinished indexing list also shows a failed section in **Delay reporting.md** with a reindex action.

![Version history, file parsing status, and unfinished indexing](../assets/northstar-knowledge-maintenance.png)

**Content changes remain traceable, parsing and indexing progress are visible separately, and maintainers can continue processing unfinished materials.**

:::tip Important

Semantic indexing status is available when the application integrates the relevant retrieval capability. Parsing one file or indexing one document does not mean all knowledge is available for answering questions. Answers still require suitable retrieved content and appropriate access. Version history does not imply automatic synchronization of external sources.

:::

url: /capabilities/template-print/index.md
---

# Template printing

Provide a business template and ask your Agent to implement document generation and download. The package provides Skills and examples; the application owns the runtime implementation.

Read the [usage guide](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/template-print/usage.md) for template preparation, authorization, and PDF conversion requirements.



---
url: /capabilities/template-print/usage.md
---

# Template printing usage guide

[← Template printing overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/template-print/index.md)

The template printing package provides an Agent Skill and reference examples. It does not include a ready-made printing interface, rendering engine, or business API. Implement generation and download in your application or business plugin.

## Prepare the template and business rules

| What to provide | Example                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A real template | A Word transport document with a company header, line items, and signature area           |
| Data sources    | The current order, customer, cargo details, and delivery information                      |
| Output format   | DOCX download; specify PDF conversion requirements if needed                              |
| Access rules    | Which roles can generate and download documents, and whether to retain generation history |

Ask the Agent to check for an existing template printing Skill. If integration is needed, follow guidance matching the application's installed version. The application owns templates, field mappings, runtime dependencies, and business code.

## Describe the requirement

```text
Generate a transport document for the current order using my Word template.
Fill in the order number, customer, origin, destination, and cargo line items, preserving the company header and signature area.
Only employees authorized to view the order may generate and download the document. Do not accept unauthorized order data supplied by the client.
Implement DOCX download first, explain how missing fields are handled, and verify the document against a real order.
If PDF is needed, identify the required conversion environment and deployment dependencies first.
```

Return to the [overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/template-print/index.md) to choose another scenario and adapt its prompt.

## Verify the result

- Check single and multiple line items, dates, amounts, and missing values against the agreed rules.
- Use accessible, authorized sources for images and QR codes.
- Enforce business permissions on generation and download APIs; changing an order identifier must not expose someone else's data.
- Open the generated document and verify PDF conversion in the actual deployment environment if it is required.

## Development references

Read the [capability package documentation](https://github.com/nocobase/nocobase/blob/v3-develop/packages/plugins/app-plugin-template-print/README.md) and the [runnable example plugin](https://github.com/nocobase/nocobase/blob/v3-develop/packages/examples/app-plugin-template-print-example/README.md). The example owns its demonstration data and routes; it is not a general-purpose printing service for every application.

url: /capabilities/approval/extension.md
---

# Extensions

This page is for developers and Agents who need integration and extension boundaries. For business design, start with [Approval overview](/nocobase-docs-vi/capabilities/approval/index.md). Use the installed approval plugin's Skill and version for detailed API contracts.

## Integrate existing records and processes

One request record identifies the complete process. `defineApproval` defines drafts, review, correction, execution, and final stages; `approvalState` adds group handling rules to a business state. Each entry creates tasks for a new round. Return and re-entry creates new tasks while preserving earlier records.

The application provides its lifecycle runtime, business tables, lifecycle storage, organization services, authentication/authorization APIs, and interface. Plugin migrations supply approval task and evidence storage. Restrict forms, imports, and APIs that directly change states or submitted fields. Contract changes and similar proposals should store requests separately from official data.

## Custom aggregation policies

Standard policies cover single, all, any, first-response, sequential, and threshold decisions. Special itemized or partial results use `StagePolicy`: declare task planning, possible outcomes, and exits. The policy calculates conclusions; the business lifecycle performs data writes.

## Custom operations and assignment rules

Use `defineApprovalAction` for abstention, returning individual items, reminders, or other business operations, explicitly registered on the relevant stages. Declare input, permissions, recipient scope, presentation, and history wording, with forms and tests. Recheck responsibility rules after transfers, added reviewers, appointment, and reassignment.

## Frozen content, outputs, and opinion reuse

`freeze` declares submitted fields. Confirmations carry the hash of the content displayed on the page. Stage outputs declare reviewer-entered amounts, dates, and similar values; write these with the business state when the conclusion is reached.

Re-entry requires fresh review by default. `reuse: 'unchanged'` reuses earlier opinions only when explicitly permitted and covered content, rule version, responsibility identities, and other conditions match. New tasks retain source evidence.

## Pages and approval centers

| Contract                            | Purpose                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `previewRoute`                      | Route preview before submission                                            |
| `runViewsFor` / `upcomingStagesFor` | Current and historical rounds, and future stages                           |
| `actionsFor` / `runActionsFor`      | Current user's task or round operations                                    |
| `candidatesFor`                     | Qualified candidates for transfer, added reviewers, and similar operations |
| `perform` / `performBatch`          | Individual actions and batch handling with per-item results                |
| `tasksOf`                           | Task aggregation; APIs still need business authorization                   |

The UI Library's `approval-ui` supplies progress, timeline, route preview, action bar, branch, and receipt components. The Agent maps server data into them; business forms and pages belong to the application. Approval centers can include other work sources, each independently authorizing reads and actions.

Administrative pages also belong to the application. Query requests, tasks, and execution records within the administrator's business scope and expose authorized appointment and reassignment. Redispatch or process reset requires business recovery exits and rules for earlier rounds; the Agent then implements administrative APIs and pages. Directly changing a state field is not a substitute for lifecycle operations.

## Notifications, deadlines, and reliable execution

The application periodically calls `ApprovalService.sweep()` for reminders, escalation, and claim expiry. `calendar` can provide working time. Connect sweeps to lifecycle background work; notifications and external calls execute after transaction commit. Partial opinions update approval tasks only. The final conclusion, business state, and next-stage tasks share a transaction.

Resource reservation/release and official data version checks belong in the business transaction. External payments, registrations, and synchronization use reliable lifecycle execution with retries, failure exits, and stable business identifiers.

## Rule versions, upgrades, and tests

Apply application migrations on upgrade, manage rule versions explicitly, and retain stages and exits used by ongoing requests. Test custom policies, operation permissions, conclusion rollback, reuse, repeated requests, concurrency, and deadlines. Test external success, explicit rejection, temporary failure, and unknown outcomes.

## Where to find extension examples

The approval example package's `server/action-examples/` contains the following extensions using public approval plugin exports. They do not appear automatically when the core plugin is installed. Register them explicitly in a business stage's `actions`, and implement forms and history wording.

| Example               | Purpose                                | Business constraints                                                   |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `urge.ts`             | Applicant reminder                     | Authorization and cooldown; notification does not change opinions      |
| `remove-signer.ts`    | Remove an added reviewer               | Only removes responsibilities the actor added, as configured           |
| `retract.ts`          | Retract an individual opinion          | Original task retains its opinion; a new task takes the fresh response |
| `terminate.ts`        | End a round                            | Explicit authorization and declared business ending exit               |
| `extend-due.ts`       | Extend deadlines                       | Changes deadlines only; declares batch support                         |
| `acknowledge.ts`      | Request and complete acknowledgement   | Paired completion operation for an auxiliary task                      |
| `abstain.ts`          | Committee abstention                   | Separate operation name; abstention is not approval                    |
| `return-item.ts`      | Return an expense line                 | Per-line outcomes and recovery rules                                   |
| `vacation-forward.ts` | Forward an absent manager's assignment | Assignment rule rather than a user operation                           |

### Integrate a custom operation

1. Define it with `defineApprovalAction()`, declaring actors, guards, availability, presentation, and effects returned by `plan()`. Do not write to the database inside planning.
2. Register it on relevant stages. Conclusion operations declare `outcomes`; the business lifecycle provides matching `approvalOutcome` exits.
3. For material or acknowledgement tasks, register a separate completion operation for recipients and define visibility and completion authority.
4. Integrate server authorization, input validation, and `perform()`. Pages use offered operations, candidates, and configuration from the server.
5. Add forms and wording in both languages. Use `registerTimelineRenderer()` for history rendering where needed. Test availability, refusal, tasks, and history changes.

### Assignment and responsibility seats

`assignees` creates one opinion per person, `subjects` one per line, and `pools` one per responsibility seat. Choose exactly one. If legal and finance teams each give one opinion, declare two pools and aggregate with `all`; do not treat every team candidate as a required voter. A pool with one candidate remains a team seat.

Default assignment rules check active status, delegation, applicant exclusion, qualifications, and duplicate responsibility. Transfers, added reviewers, and reassignment are also checked. Transfers and added reviewers require recipient scopes. Replacing the whole assignment chain assumes responsibility for all these constraints; usually compose business rules with the defaults.

### Consistency and retries

The final opinion, round closure, business transition, and next-stage tasks should share one transaction. External calls execute after commit; do not perform bank payments directly within the approval transaction. `perform()` uses a stable `requestId`, with retries retaining action, identity, and target. `performBatch()` returns success or failure per item rather than using one transaction for all requests.

Submit the hash of content displayed on the page with the opinion. Do not silently fetch the newest hash when the user approves, hiding content they have not reviewed. Attachment replacement, related data versions, and historical form reconstruction need additional business storage and validation contracts.

### Background time rules

In the Provider that creates the lifecycle runtime, connect `createLifecycleJobs()`: `onSweep` calls approval `sweep()` and lifecycle `prune()`, while effects also run through jobs. The plugin starts no timer itself. Multi-process production applications should use shared jobs storage so each process does not run an independent memory queue.

The current contract example provides working time in UTC+8, Monday–Friday 09:00–18:00, used for manager deadlines and procurement claim expiry, without a holiday table. The lab sweep processes tasks already due; it does not advance time. Use a controlled clock for precise timeout boundaries. Shared pause and handover deadline rules still need business decisions.

Applicant recusal is enabled by default. When business authorization explicitly permits self-approval, set `allowSelfApproval: true` on the relevant stage, for example a budget owner confirming their own purchase before independent finance review. This permits an eligible applicant to decide manually, including through delegation; it does not auto-approve or skip the stage, and other assignment rules and action permissions still apply. The applicant is the identity returned by `applicant(record)`, which may differ from a proxy submitter. Do not replace the entire assignment chain to enable this policy.
